notes.text: The author states that d commutes with the L_0 operations, using the action letter on L_1 and inner automorphisms on L_0, and writes the separate compatibility equation with inner automorphisms of L_1. These statements are transcribed as written.

The paragraph asserts that Im d is invariant in L_0, that Coker d = pi_0 is defined, that pi_1 = Ker d is central in L_1, and that L_0 acts on L_1 en invariant pi_1, followed by et qu’il opère via pi_0. The exact wording and its antecedent are retained; no extra restriction to pi_1 is supplied.

The interlinear coh. qualifies invariant. The named invariant is followed by alpha in H^3(pi_0,pi_1), with a separately doubtful point after membership. The name’s penultimate vowel remains uncertain.

The author says he has encountered these structures in various situations and has again met them in the classification of ordinary formal groups over a perfect field, involving affine algebraic groups and commutative formal groups linked by strict Gr-structures. The quotation concerning the transcendent character begins on this page and is unfinished.

The legible note refers to ce formalisme sur un topos quelconque (pas seulement dans (Ens)). The depleted outer line cannot supply a recoverable French clause. Its connector indicates the neighbourhood of the strictes line without fixing an exact insertion point.

Author page 5 is at top centre. Archive foliation 150 is represented only as a comment. H’s 149 is packet/editorial pagination and is not imported as the author’s page number. There is no date, new salutation, closing, explicit question, or author’s avowed mathematical doubt on this sheet; évidemment is the author’s own assertion.

The action-letter case, every x and L index, every pi occurrence, the int/Im/Ker/Coker letterforms, the dot after d, both parentheses around the argument in b), membership versus epsilon shape, H font, raised 3, argument comma, and the nested parentheses around Ens were checked from their own strokes. Mathematical expectations did not replace the written forms.

No mathematical proof, re-proof, computation or formal verification was performed. These are visual transcription inspections, so the checks list is empty. No other page, reader, source, OCR, browsing or LaTeX compilation was used.

coverage: The whole page was viewed once for layout and dimensions, then half a and half b once each, in that order. Every physical prose line, all three displays, each separate mathematical occurrence, both labels, the interlinear coh., the small cancelled sign, overtraced words, both underlines, quotation marks, author number and archive foliation were read against the complete C and H texts; witness agreement was not treated as evidence. Sixteen tight crops were made only for unresolved places, using the supplied crop.py with width 2800 and the sideways note rotated -90 degrees. Each crop was viewed once. Exact original-source boxes are provided for changed and reviewed loci, including half-settled punctuation and both sides of the Postnikoff-Sinh line break. H omits the small cancelled sign, the dot after d in b), the doubtful cohomology point and the comma after affines; its alleged separate deletion before sur cannot be isolated as a separate word. C’s insertion treatment of the note is replaced by a margin note, and its page-final du is read des. H already acknowledges the unreadable marginal opening and both page numbers in editorial notes, so these are not claimed as H omissions. The final reading remains complete through the unfinished final word and does not supply continuation text.
